red/sledy-na-vode/34/laerta: Rodrigo da Vira, navigator aboard the [[santa-eliza|Santa Eliza]], leaves Laerta on the expedition to Solanta. This is revealed in ch. 34.
red/sledy-na-vode/34/solanta: The doge demands the man who knows the channel. Carlos hands over da Vira, who is held in a Solantian prison and sold into slavery.
red/sledy-na-vode/4/dunkvald: The Catalian is brought in bonds to the forest camp of enslaved diggers. Joriksen promises freedom for a schönbrun.
red/sledy-na-vode/8/dunkvald: Winter in the dugout: the Sorge um dich rite, the fight with the foreman, and the equal division of food.
red/sledy-na-vode/12/dunkvald: Water at the thirteenth yard. Greta is the “prize” in place of freedom, and Red flees into the forest.
red/sledy-na-vode/15/dunkvald: Yakka brings back the fugitive. The letter goes to Laerta, and Red digs by night, singing.
red/sledy-na-vode/19/dunkvald: Red’s cough is gone. The foreman buries him alive in the pit.
red/sledy-na-vode/23/dunkvald: The sarcoma is gone. Red recovers at Greta’s house and digs again.
red/sledy-na-vode/27/dunkvald: Täuschung: a slaughter on the road, and Landau seizes Red with an unknown power.
red/sledy-na-vode/33/dunkvald: Years of executions in the pit, the “THOU SHALT NOT KILL” brand, and Red is taken into the army.
red/sledy-na-vode/33/ollandiya: In the army Red is Neubiy, a “stone” rifleman attached to [[ditrikh|Dietrich’s]] battery in ch. 2. The platoon of stones flees at night.
red/sledy-na-vode/34/tres-molinos: Da Vira and the Dangarian deserters live in the House Above with van Halm. He makes a dark schönbrun and takes revenge on the heroes of Solanta.
ditrikh/sledy-na-vode/2/ollandiya: The battery behind the Ollandian lines: three volleys of grapeshot.
ditrikh/sledy-na-vode/6/latsen: Interrogation by Major Klein at headquarters.
ditrikh/sledy-na-vode/29/khofshtadt: Joriksen demands that they leave at once. In the compartment, Magnus Amir the Grey tells of the destruction of Dunkwald.
ditrikh/sledy-na-vode/31/latsen: Back in Ollandia: arrested at Latsen station on Klein’s orders, then released.
